question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A leopard cannot change its spots

options.text: A dangerous animal can be hunted
A person must hide his weaknesses
A wild animal can be tamed
A person cannot change his basic nature

explanation: A leopard cannot change its spots = व्यक्ति का मूल स्वभाव नहीं बदलता। Example: He promised to reform, but a leopard cannot change its spots.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be on the warpath

options.text: To be angry and ready for a fight
To lead an army to peace talks

explanation: On the warpath = लड़ने को आमादा, ग़ुस्से में। Example: The principal was on the warpath after the cheating.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To eat one's heart out

options.text: To suffer silently from grief or envy

explanation: Eat one's heart out = भीतर ही भीतर कुढ़ना। Example: She ate her heart out when her friend won the prize.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fly off the handle

options.text: To leave a job in haste

explanation: Fly off the handle = अचानक आपे से बाहर हो जाना। Example: He flies off the handle at the slightest delay.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To have a soft spot for

options.text: To have a special fondness for

explanation: Have a soft spot for = के प्रति विशेष लगाव रखना। Example: The teacher has a soft spot for shy students.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep mum
explanation: Keep mum = चुप्पी साधे रखना। Example: He kept mum about the plan.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To look daggers at

options.text: To stare at someone with great anger

explanation: Look daggers at = ग़ुस्से से घूरना। Example: She looked daggers at him for breaking the vase.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make a beeline for

options.text: To go straight and quickly towards
To follow a long winding path

explanation: Make a beeline for = सीधा और तेज़ी से उसी ओर जाना। Example: The children made a beeline for the ice-cream stall.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To mend fences
explanation: Mend fences = बिगड़े रिश्ते सुधारना। Example: The minister travelled to mend fences with the allies.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To open a can of worms

options.text: To create a complicated problem by raising a sensitive matter

explanation: Open a can of worms = पेचीदा मुसीबत खड़ी कर देना। Example: Questioning the old accounts opened a can of worms.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pass the hat round

options.text: To give away one's old clothes
To collect money from a group of people
To wear a hat in public

explanation: Pass the hat round = चंदा इकट्ठा करना। Example: We passed the hat round to help the injured worker.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pick holes in

options.text: To dig a pit in the ground

explanation: Pick holes in = कमियाँ निकालना। Example: Critics picked holes in the new policy.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To put one's foot down
explanation: Put one's foot down = सख़्ती से अपनी बात पर अड़ जाना। Example: Father put his foot down about late-night parties.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To put one's foot in it

options.text: To make an embarrassing mistake by saying something tactless

explanation: Put one's foot in it = बेतुकी बात कहकर शर्मिंदा होना। Example: He put his foot in it by asking about her failed marriage.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To raise the roof

options.text: To make a very loud noise, especially by cheering or celebrating

explanation: Raise the roof = शोर-शराबे से आसमान सिर पर उठा लेना। Example: The fans raised the roof when India won.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To save one's skin

options.text: To protect oneself from the sun
To earn a lot of money

explanation: Save one's skin = अपनी जान या इज़्ज़त बचा लेना। Example: He blamed his friend to save his skin.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To see red

options.text: To become suddenly and extremely angry

explanation: See red = आग-बबूला हो जाना। Example: He saw red when he read the insulting letter.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To shed crocodile tears

options.text: To weep for a lost friend

explanation: Shed crocodile tears = घड़ियाली आँसू बहाना। Example: The heir shed crocodile tears at the funeral.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To show one's true colours
explanation: Show one's true colours = असली चेहरा दिखाना। Example: He showed his true colours when the money ran out.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To stick to one's guns

options.text: To refuse to change one's opinion despite pressure

explanation: Stick to one's guns = अपनी बात पर डटे रहना। Example: She stuck to her guns despite the criticism.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take a rain check

options.text: To politely postpone an offer to a later time

explanation: Take a rain check = न्योते को बाद के लिए टाल देना। Example: I can't come today; may I take a rain check?

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take someone to task

options.text: To scold someone for a fault

explanation: Take someone to task = फटकारना, जवाबदेही माँगना। Example: The boss took him to task for the delay.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To tighten one's belt
explanation: Tighten one's belt = ख़र्चों में कटौती करना। Example: After the pay cut, we had to tighten our belts.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To turn the tables

options.text: To reverse a situation to one's advantage

explanation: Turn the tables = बाज़ी पलट देना। Example: The new bowler turned the tables in the last over.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To wash one's hands of

options.text: To refuse to take any further responsibility for

explanation: Wash one's hands of = पल्ला झाड़ लेना। Example: The manager washed his hands of the failed project.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To wear one's heart on one's sleeve

options.text: To wear a badge with pride

explanation: Wear one's heart on one's sleeve = मन की भावनाएँ खुलकर ज़ाहिर करना। Example: She wears her heart on her sleeve.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To win hands down

options.text: To win after a hard fight

explanation: Win hands down = आसानी से जीत जाना। Example: Our team won hands down.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A skeleton in the cupboard
explanation: A skeleton in the cupboard = घर का छिपा हुआ शर्मनाक राज़। Example: Every old family has a skeleton in the cupboard.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A snake in the grass

options.text: A hidden enemy or a treacherous person

explanation: A snake in the grass = आस्तीन का साँप। Example: He proved to be a snake in the grass.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A fool's paradise

options.text: A state of happiness based on false hopes

explanation: A fool's paradise = झूठी उम्मीदों पर टिकी ख़ुशी, ख़्याली जन्नत। Example: He lives in a fool's paradise, thinking the exam is easy.
